answer: A durable sybil defense for an agent economy is to tie identity and reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than cheap registrations. Picture a violet trellis: each agent climbs by producing attestations others can check, and trust spreads like a ripple only from nodes that have already earned weight. New entrants must stake effort before their votes count, so flooding the network with fake identities stops paying off, since each clone dilutes its own influence and the cost of proving genuine participation outweighs any gain.
